scope: All checks below judge world-scenario captures. Exception - synthetic probe: if EVERY frame in the reel shows only bare geometric primitives on an empty void (no tilemap, no HUD bars, no controls strip, no banner text anywhere in the reel), the replay is a render-pipeline smoke (e.g. moving_square) and each check whose subject cannot exist in such a probe passes with why='synthetic probe, out of scope'. no_render_garbage still applies in full - tearing or corrupted output fails even in a probe. If even ONE frame shows a tilemap or HUD, no exemption applies.

checks.check: Pack creatures (warm orange family) and humans (pale bone) are immediately distinguishable from each other and from the floor in every frame where both appear.

The three pack creatures read as three DIFFERENT kinds (bright ember orange / deep rust / pale amber), not three copies. If no frame shows all three, judge from the frames that show two. If no frame shows at least two pack creatures, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

In frames with multiple pack creatures, exactly one reads as 'the one I control': it stands on a soft warm-GOLD ground halo (an ellipse under its feet with a brighter rim) and a small gold chevron floats just above its head. No other body carries the halo or the chevron. If no frame shows more than one pack creature, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Across the swap frames, the gold ground halo + chevron appear under/over a DIFFERENT pack creature before vs after - possession visibly moved. If the reel never shows the halo on two different creatures (single-body scenes, off-camera swap targets), pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

A body reads which way it faces in a static frame from the SPRITE itself: facing the camera shows the face/eyes and the weapon hand; facing away shows the back of the head/hood/helmet with no face; a side profile shows one eye and the weapon arm in front. Monsters read facing by their head/dart/eye side. A small dark notch on the faced edge is optional, not required. Fail only if bodies read as directionless blobs.
At least one frame shows a small pale shot in flight, clearly separate from any creature body. If the script never fires a projectile, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Human attack telegraph (red edge + yellow core swell) reads as incoming danger and is clearly distinct from the gold gate/transition tiles.. If no telegraph frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'

No pack creature's damage flash reads as WHITE (white reads as a spawn/holy effect); pack hurt-flash must read crimson/red. Judge only frames where a pack creature is mid-flash; if none, mark pass=true with why='not exercised'.

In at least one frame after a kill, a faded remnant of the fallen body is visible where it fell (fights leave history). The remnant reads as a pale warm patch carrying a thin near-black rim that separates it from the floor greys — a remnant melting invisibly into bare floor fails. A drop marker legitimately spawns ON the death tile and may cover most of the remnant: where a post-kill frame shows a drop marker with a lighter fringe (with or without its rim visible) hugging its edges on the death tile, that fringe IS the remnant and passes. FAIL only when a post-kill death tile shows bare floor with no drop marker and no remnant. If no post-kill frame exists, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

The HUD is a translucent dark PANEL top-left: three rows, each a small portrait box (the kit's face) beside a kit-colored hp bar with a dark edge; the possessed one is wider, framed in GOLD, and carries its hp numeral (n/max) at the bar's right end. Bars plausibly track the fight shown. A downed body's bar (flat dark, no kit-colored fill) carries a thin warm hairline outline separating it from the field behind it — a dead bar melting invisibly into dark ground fails; live bars carry no such hairline (their kit fill and backing carry them). If no frame shows a downed body's bar, judge the rest of this check as usual.

Nest frames (warm dark organic) and district frames (ZONE 2, descent floor -1: a dark canyon of tan rock walls with two themed halves split by a near-black chasm) read as different places at a glance.

When ZONE 2 frames show ground on both sides of the central chasm (or the reel crosses it), the two halves read as two different biomes of one floor, never one flat fill: ground character (moss density, tone, openness) visibly differs across the void, and in mid-map latitudes (the bridge-2/3 band) the EAST half carries the dense green moss belt. FAIL if both sides read as the same flat ground. If the reel never shows both halves, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the central chasm band of ZONE 2 is on camera (a wide dark navy column running the map's length, a lighter shallow rim where it meets the tan rock, faint still ripple streaks and shimmer inside), it reads as a DEEP FLOOD the pack does not enter: clearly darker than any walkable ground, bounded by the rock with a curved shore, and no body ever stands inside it in any frame. Water texture is expected (it IS water); fail only if a pack body stands in the band or if the band is indistinguishable from walkable floor. If no chasm frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a ZONE 2 bridge is on camera (a straight warm-tan plank band spanning the chasm), it reads as a BUILT CROSSING: warmer and lighter than every surrounding ground family, running edge-to-edge across the void. In frames where a body stands mid-bridge, the void reads on BOTH sides of the bridge band - the crossing is a commitment, not a floor. If no bridge frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.
No frame shows tearing, missing map, entities outside walls, or obviously corrupted output.
If a wipe frame is present, it reads as a run-ending event (dark veil + large text), distinct from ordinary combat frames. If the script never wipes, mark pass=true with why='not exercised'.

When special frames are present, Blocker reads as a heavy ring shock, Lobber as delayed targeted tiles, and Striker as a bright ring burst (brighter/whiter family than the Blocker's warm ring). The three effects must not look like one reused attack effect. If this replay has no special frames, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When Volley target tiles are present, their pack-orange outlined countdown is clearly different from both the human red-edge/yellow-core danger telegraph and the solid gold zone gate. If absent, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.
When a pack mark is present, one human has a clear reticle glyph that does not resemble the gold possession halo/chevron or attack tiles. If absent, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

All three HUD bars have a stable special pip. When special casts are present, the relevant body's pip visibly changes from ready to spent while the other bodies retain their own state; if no special is cast in this replay, pass based on all three pips being present and note that tracking was not exercised.

When glean drops are present, they read as GEMS: small DIAMOND shapes (not squares) standing on a tile, bobbing slightly, with a facet highlight and a brief white sparkle; magenta/violet near the descent mouth, warm-rose or ember-gold with a soft cross-shaped glow deeper across the floor. Their diamond silhouette and motion make them clearly distinct from corpses, projectiles, the square human telegraph frame, the teal mark reticle, and the flat gold gate slab. A near-expiry drop fades (decay, not a render bug). If this replay shows no drops, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

The possessed HUD bar row reserves a slot at its right end (right of the two pips) for a small magenta carried numeral. Where that numeral is present it reads there and ONLY there - a carried-style numeral in the bottom-edge controls strip (key/action reference text only) or anywhere else on the HUD fails; a thin dark halo separates it from whatever world pixels scroll behind it (raw halo-less purple melting into a light wall fails); where it is absent the bar layout reads identical minus the numeral (no layout shift). Absence alone is never a failure: carried value strands on the body's corpse at death and leaves at banking, so a reel can honestly show no carried numeral despite earlier pickups - and center-screen ledger tally panels or station-anchored numerals are NOT carried readouts (their own rows judge them). If no frame shows the carried numeral, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When nest frames include the station fixture (hollow-centered magenta-toned block), it reads as a distinct interactable place â€” not a wall, not the gold gate. When the possessed stands within ~3 tiles of it, a banked-total numeral is legible above the fixture; station-anchored numerals (banked totals and -N prices) carry a thin dark halo that keeps them readable where they cross light ground (walls, bodies) — a raw halo-less purple numeral melting into light ground fails. If the replay never shows the station, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Taunted humans are marked by a thin deep-rust underline strip BELOW the body (offset clear of the red-edge attack telegraph), distinct from the telegraph flare, the hurt flash, the teal mark reticle corners, and magenta drops. A near-expiry underline may read faded â€” that is decay, not a bug. Humans crowding a pack body WITHOUT underlines are ordinary nearest-targeting, NOT taunt â€” do not infer taunt from a swarm. Judge only if at least one frame shows the expanding rust square cast pulse or an underlined human; otherwise pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a taunt cast frame is present, it shows ONE continuous expanding hollow rust SQUARE outline centered on the deep-rust pack creature, clearly distinct from the solid pale special/damage tiles, the orange volley target brackets, and the human telegraph. If no cast frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a mid-taunt frame is present, multiple humans are adjacent to or converging on the deep-rust (blocker) body â€” the rust-underlined humans cluster around IT and not around any other pack body. The blocker anchoring the swarm may legitimately BE the possessed white-ringed body (a self-anchor cast is the taunt working as designed). The failure case is rust-underlined humans swarming a NON-blocker pack body while the blocker stands ignored. If no mid-taunt frame with multiple living taunted humans exists, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

A loaded pack corpse is marked by a hollow magenta OUTLINE pip centered on the container's TILE. The pip may legitimately sit up to one tile BESIDE the brown corpse rectangle - a knockback kill leaves the body's pixels trailing off its committed tile, and the pip marks the interact tile, not the sprite (this offset is correct, not a defect). Judge instead: the pip is a hollow OUTLINE, distinct from free drops (small FILLED magenta squares), the bank station, and looted/expired corpses (no pip anywhere near them) - INCLUDING in any frame where a free drop and a hollow outline share a tile (filled square inside a hollow outline = two objects). If no loaded corpse appears, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Across the replay's frames, loaded (full-strength body + pip), looted-empty (no pip, body fading), and expired (no pip, body fading, or a brief dark tile flash) pack corpses read as three DIFFERENT states, and a settling corpse (dim pip) reads distinct from a lootable one (full pip). Judge only the states the frames actually show; if fewer than two states appear, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When post-wipe frames are present AND a loaded corpse with a pip exists in the district, the return frames read as a purposeful RETURN: the pack re-entering the district while at least one loaded corpse with a pip awaits. Do not infer a corpse run from mere walking; require a visible pip in the district frames. If the script has no wipe followed by a return to a district holding a loaded corpse, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

After combat ends, a large glyph+number tally appears center-screen above the player avatar on a dark contrast panel (filled magenta square + a +N number in large bold type; optionally loss and net lines under it) and later fades out. It must be one of the most visually prominent on-screen elements during its display - comparable in scale to the zone banner or wipe text. Gains (magenta) must read distinct from losses (a hollow outline glyph with -N, or a dark red-edged square with -N). If no tally appears in these frames, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a tally shows a loss line, judge the net by tally kind. Fight/wipe tallies (mid-combat, or over the wipe veil): the net includes stranded + destroyed value, so with a loss line present the net line reads clearly NEGATIVE ('= -N', red family). Bank tallies (at the station, trip reconciliation): the hollow outline -N is OUTSTANDING value waiting on corpses and is deliberately NOT in the bank net — a positive '= +N' (magenta) beside a hollow -N is CORRECT there; a bank net reads negative (red) only when dark destroyed losses exceed the take. Any net whose sign and color disagree (a negative amount in positive magenta, or a positive amount in red) fails. If no tally with a loss line appears, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

During the wipe veil (dark overlay), the tally renders OVER the veil and stays legible - its numbers readable against the darkened field. The hollow-outline loss number is the value waiting on corpses out in the world. If no wipe with a live tally appears, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the pack banks at the station, a tally appears center-screen above the player avatar on a dark contrast panel, reading as a trip reconciliation: a +N take in large bold type, optionally a hollow-outline -N (value still out on corpses) and a net line. It must be visually prominent - large type on a panel, comparable to the zone banner. It must be distinguishable from mid-fight tallies by context (station present, no combat). If no banking tally appears, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a fight tally or bank tally is on screen, it reads as one of the TWO OR THREE most visually prominent elements in the frame - its type size and dark panel make it impossible to miss, comparable in visual weight to the 64pt wipe text or the zone banner. A player focused on the center of the screen CANNOT fail to notice it. The tally must NOT read as a small footnote, marginal annotation, or debug overlay. If no tally appears in these frames, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When pressuring humans are visible (thin hollow outline stance, distinct from the filled-body engaged humans that are actively attacking), the group reads as ENCIRCLEMENT - bodies positioned around the pack creature at a fixed perimeter distance, waiting. They must NOT read as laggy or broken pathing; the formation must look deliberate and menacing. Pressuring humans are visually distinct from engaged humans (engaged = red-edge telegraph active, body adjacent, attacking; pressuring = outline only, perimeter spacing, no telegraph). If no frame shows pressuring humans distinct from engaged ones, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the reel leaves a zone while humans are displaced off their posts (an early frame showing humans at rest positions, then a chase frame showing them pulled toward the pack) and re-enters that zone later: on the FIRST re-entry frame the previously-chasing humans stand NEITHER at the chase positions they were last seen at NOR back at their original rest posts - they read as caught partway along the way home. Across later frames the interrupted walk completes: a subsequent re-entry or later frame shows those humans back at their original posts. The dead-teleport tell - humans standing exactly at their far posts on the very first re-entry frame after a brief absence - fails this check. A placed human turning back toward the pack instead of finishing its walk is the same law read honestly (dispersed, not invulnerable) and does not fail this check. If the reel never re-enters a zone with previously-displaced humans, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a human walks home after losing its target (leash disengage), the movement reads as INTENTIONAL RETREAT - a creature turning away and walking back toward its home tile, not as broken AI or stuck pathing. The walkback is visually distinct from pursuit: the human moves AWAY from the pack rather than toward it. If multiple frames show the same human at different positions during a walkback, the trajectory reads as smooth and purposeful. If no frame captures a human mid-walkback (moving away from pack toward its spawn), pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

ZONE 2's threat grows AWAY from the descent mouth (the south-west landing pocket): frames taken deep in the floor (across bridges, the east half, or the far north) show more hostile presence than frames at the mouth landing, which reads as a calm arrival pocket (no hostiles adjacent on arrival). Hostiles cluster in ARENA GROUPS (camp/grove pockets) with watchers along the trails - grouped occupation, not an even smear. If the script does not include both mouth-landing and deep-floor frames for comparison, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a pack body carries the god-mark (a small hollow pale-gold square floating just above the body), it reads at a glance as a persistent blessing on THAT body â€” clearly distinct from the white possession ring (full-body outline), the teal mark reticle (on humans), and magenta drop/pip glyphs. A thin near-black outline frames the mark's quad, separating it from whatever ground it floats over — a pale mark melting edge-less into a light wall fails. If no marked body appears in this replay, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

In nest frames showing the stations, the three fixtures read as three DIFFERENT interactable places (bank magenta-toned, altar pale bone-gold, vat green) â€” a stranger could point at which is which. None reads as a wall or the gold gate. If fewer than two fixtures appear, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a tribute fires at the vat (dead bodies regrow at the spawn tiles, wounded HP bars refill), the before/after frames read as a purchase: bodies that were missing/dead stand alive near the vat afterward, and the station cue pulse marks the transaction. Regrown bodies are persistent state â€” judge any post-tribute frame. If no tribute occurs in this replay, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

POST-wipe return frames (first frames after the veil lifts) show the judgment: marked bodies stand at the nest spawn while dissolved bodies are ABSENT (their HP bars read dead/empty), or â€” in the floor case â€” exactly one kept vessel stands alone. The return must NOT show all three bodies alive after a wipe in which fewer than three were marked. If no wipe occurs in this replay, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a human switches targets mid-fight, a brief small block flashes above it, its color keyed to the cause (rust=kit-hate, yellow=wounded-prey, pale=proximity steal) â€” readable as 'it turned for a reason', distinct from the telegraph flare and hurt flash. A thin near-black outline frames the cue block so its boundary reads on any ground (the dark rust cue may still read quiet on dark floors — recorded residual, not a failure; a LIGHT cue melting edge-less into a light wall fails). If no retarget cue frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the reel stages a GENUINE separation - a frame where a living ally's body clearly sits beyond the viewport edge (the possessed has visibly traveled away from the pack mid-reel) - a small kit-colored square pip clamped at the viewport edge toward that ally must read, framed by a thin near-black outline that keeps it visible on any ground. The pip must not be confusable with drops (world-anchored, magenta/rose/gold family): edge pips hug the viewport boundary and wear kit colors. Counting HUD bars against visible bodies is NOT evidence of off-screen-ness: at spawn and in tight formations allies stand adjacent (and may be partially covered by the bottom controls strip) while fully on-screen. If no frame stages an unambiguous off-screen ally, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a deep-district drop (ember/gold square, larger than the magenta drops, with a faint glow halo) is on camera, it reads visibly RICHER than near-gate drops (small magenta) â€” a stranger could point at which is worth more, even in a frame showing only the gold drop. When a mid-band drop (warm rose, sized between the two) is also present, it reads BETWEEN them: bigger and warmer than magenta, smaller and quieter than gold. If no ember/gold drop appears in this replay, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the seal is on camera SEALED, it reads as a shut, priced door: a dark slab across the corridor with a thin gold seam, the seal station beside it, and a visible price â€” a stranger could say 'locked, costs money'. When the breach beat is on camera, the way visibly OPENS (the slab turns gold) and the line 'TOLL PAID' is legible in the banner slot; where the TOLL PAID line and a zone-name banner are live in the same frame, the two lines read as two separate lines with clear air between them (breach ink striking through or touching the zone-name line fails). If no seal or breach frame is present in this replay, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When frames show the grass fixture zone (ZONE 6: a green tile field on the west side, a brown dirt path, a gray stone plaza, and a warm wood platform east), the grass field reads as AUTHORED variation - at least two visibly different green tones patchworked across the field's tiles (not one flat green fill, and not noise or corruption), and the four ground families (grass, dirt, stone, wood) read as four different materials at a glance. Tile boundaries read through the materials themselves (edges, faces, foam) — the old grid lines are OFF by design (MUNDO VIVO FASE 3, D7), their absence is not a defect. If no grass-fixture frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a camp ('HUB 1') or ZONE 3 (district_two) banner frame is on camera, the banner text is legible and the zone reads distinct from ZONE 2 (district) at a glance: the camp reads safe, station-dense, and warm (warm-gray walls, ember braziers at the wall clusters); ZONE 3 reads as a SUBMERGED open plain - dark blue-grey seabed under rust-brown boundary rock, with a vivid deep-blue channel and orange coral visible wherever the camera nears the water. If neither zone appears in this replay, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a striker special-active frame is present, the burst reads as ONE area hit: bright ring tiles around the striker with at least one adjacent victim reacting in the same frame (hurt flash or displaced outward) OR an adjacent victim visibly deleted by the burst across the reel (alive in a pre-burst frame, corpse/absent in the burst frames - a one-shot kill is the burst landing). If no striker special is exercised in this script, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a blocker challenge frame window is present (the expanding square pulse), the room visibly answers it: at least one human in the pulse carries the rust taunt underline or has turned to face the blocker within the pulse's read window. If no blocker special is exercised in this script, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

A quiet strip at the bottom edge of the screen shows key glyphs paired with action labels for the currently possessed body. Both halves of each pair read legibly against the strip's dark band — action labels melting into the backing fail — while key glyphs still read a notch brighter than their labels (reference hierarchy: keys pop, verbs stay quieter). The strip updates when possession changes (a different vessel name/verb appears). A brief brighter pulse may accompany the first possession of a kind (allowed, not required). The strip reads as instructional reference, NOT as a combat element — its alpha is subdued relative to the HUD bars and the ledger tally. If the script never shows a living possessed body, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a respawn tell is active (a pulsing ground indicator on a floor tile, pale green-white family), it reads as 'something is about to arrive HERE' — clearly distinct from the human attack telegraph (red-edge/yellow-core), volley impact brackets (orange), the gold gate tiles, and the taunt pulse (rust square). The tell grows or brightens over its visible lifetime and a human materializes at the tell tile at or after full intensity (a tell may legitimately HOLD at full intensity while the player stands near — deferral is honest waiting, not a defect). If no respawn tell frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a DUNGEON 1 frame is on camera (the serpent geometry: a near-black blue VOID fills all non-walkable space as solid tiles, a root-brown coiled band of walkable ground with sand/grass/dirt flecks, a pale cement core with a cross of walkways at the center): the void reads as a second, darker wall class distinct from any rock, and the coil reads as ONE continuous serpent body, not scattered islands. If no DUNGEON 1 frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the boss's (BOSS 1) chant is on camera, a deep-blue expanding hollow ring centers on ONE pale human and a small hollow blue square floats above exactly one pack vessel — the pair reads as 'he is calling THAT body', clearly distinct from the rust taunt square, the teal respawn tell, the red/yellow attack telegraph, the orange volley brackets, AND the small washed-out pale-blue retarget cue block (the chant family is deeper and more saturated, and body-scale rather than an 8px block). Wherever the boss himself is on camera, his small cream BOSS 1 nameplate above the body reads separated from the ground behind it by a thin dark halo — raw cream glyphs melting into pale walls fail. The boss is identified ONLY by his cream BOSS 1 nameplate over a pale-bone human body — a pink or red-tinted mushroom/jellyfish body is a hurt-flashing hostile, never the boss. If no chant frame and no nameplated boss body is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a seized vessel is on camera, it carries a thin blue underline (mirror of the rust taunt underline) and a body-scale blue darkening for the whole hold and, in the stamp frames, the lines BOSS 1 SPAWNED / BOSS 1 DEFEATED are legible in the banner slot with banner-scale prominence. A seized body standing adjacent to the boss doing nothing is the design, not broken AI. If neither a seized vessel nor a challenger stamp appears, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the reel crosses two or more zones, each zone reads as a DIFFERENT PLACE by floor/wall palette and landmark features alone (hue family, sparse floor motif, authored landmarks like braziers, drowned stains, or channel-lip edges) — you could tell the frames apart with the banner covered. Value structure stays constant everywhere: floor dark, walls lighter, gold strictly reserved for open ways. If the reel never leaves one zone, pass with why='not exercised by this script'. Zone COUNT is judged by the zone names the banners show, not by crossings: a reel whose every zone banner names the SAME zone (e.g. TEST 1 throughout — the test fixture's level-gated way loops back into its own zone) never left one zone, and 'not exercised' applies no matter how many gate crossings occur.

Event stamps (gate-gold lines like BOSS 1 DEFEATED / MARK LOST) LAND like stamps: framed by a thin top+bottom gold rule pair, and where consecutive frames straddle a stamp's arrival the text is visibly larger in the earlier frame (scale-in settling). Located stamps (seal breach at its station, boss defeated, mark lost) also press a gold floor seal mark — a small rect frame with an inner glyph — at the event tile, fading with the banner. Zone name banners stay quiet (bone, no rules — zone banners announce, event stamps land emphatic). If no event stamp appears, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

A death on camera POPS: the corpse tile flashes solid bright for the first frames after the kill (the primary channel) and small warm shards fly outward from the death tile (secondary, motion read). Kill-evidence across the reel counts: a victim alive in one frame and flashing/shattered or absent in the next IS the pop landing. If no death lands on camera in this script, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

While the boss's chant runs, a thin chant-blue square writ-frame centers on him and the world OUTSIDE that frame darkens hard while everything INSIDE (the chant ring, the boss, nearby bodies, the possessed's white ring) stays fully readable — dread without unfairness: no threat inside the writ may be obscured, and the HUD/controls strip stay legible over the darkening. If no chant frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

In EVERY frame where the bottom controls strip is visible, a U/R potion pair sits in the strip (after swap, seventh pair) AND a POTION N counter reads at the strip's right edge — N may be 0, and zero stock MUST read as POTION 0, never as absence. A strip frame missing either the pair or the counter FAILS. If no frame in the reel shows the controls strip at all, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

A potion buy or use flashes the bright 1-tile pulse ring at the presser's tile with a functional text line (POTION BOUGHT / POTION USED) one row above it, readable against the floor. If the script never buys or uses a potion, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

A refused sustain press (at cap, broke, or at full health) shows a dark-red X-bar drawn OVER the presser's body plus a REFUSED text line above the tile - the refusal must never read as nothing-happened. The REFUSED line reads pale cream type on a small dark backing chip hugging its own padded line box - raw backing-less red caps melting into the ground fail. If the script never stages a sustain refusal, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

In frames where a burst or AoE effect is active (striker ring burst, blocker ring shock / challenge pulse, lobber volley impacts, kill-pop shards), the spectacle stays inside its legibility budget: actor silhouettes (pack bodies, humans, the possessed's white ring) and the ground state around the effect (floor tiles, drops, pips, corpses, telegraphs, gold ways) remain readable. An effect may briefly cover its own tiles, but it must never white-out or flood the play-space so that you cannot tell where bodies stand or what lies on the ground under or beside it. The wipe veil and the boss writ-frame darkening are NOT bursts and are exempt. If no burst/AoE frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Beneath the three kit hp bars a LEVEL label with a thin gold progress bar (tick marks along its bottom) reads inside the HUD panel in every frame showing the HUD; under it a coin disc + COINS numeral and a flask + POTION numeral read as two small chips; at level 1 with no XP the bar may be empty but its dark backing still frames it; the fill never overflows the backing; the strip never reads as a fourth hp bar (it is far thinner, gold rather than kit-colored, and attached to its LEVEL label).

Where consecutive frames straddle a level-up: a gate-gold stamp reading LEVEL <N> lands with the rule-pair stamp grammar, gold shards fly outward from each living pack body's tile, and these gold pops read distinctly from the white-flash kill pop at the victim tile. The HUD strip's level numeral is higher and its bar shorter in the post-dwell frame than pre-kill. If the reel contains no level-up, or no consecutive capture pair straddles one, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where a Lobber volley telegraph is present AND the HUD level strip reads 5 or higher: the bracket chain spans FOUR contiguous tiles starting two ahead of the caster (not the three-tile base chain) - judge the span in the clearest mid-delay frame; a victim's body legitimately covers the bracket it stands on. Where captures straddle the impact with a victim standing at the FARTHEST bracket, the impact resolves there: that tile shows the kill flash or hurt reaction in the straddling frame and the chain is gone from it. If no volley telegraph appears, or the HUD reads below LEVEL 5, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where a LEVEL N REQUIRED text line shows above a way tile: the line reads pale cream type on a small dark backing chip hugging its own padded line box (raw backing-less red caps fail; the X-bar below it stays dark red), the named N exceeds the number on the HUD LEVEL strip in that same frame, and that way is shut - in frames where the refusal cue is live, its red X-bar and any standing body legitimately cover the slab's thin gold seam, but the tile still reads dark slab, never solid walkable gold; in at least one frame without the cue the same shut way shows the full slab-with-thin-gold-seam grammar. Where a later frame shows the HUD LEVEL at or above that N, the same way draws open walkable gold with no requirement line above it. If no LEVEL-N-REQUIRED line appears anywhere in the reel, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where a menu panel is on camera (a dimming veil over the whole frame with a near-black panel titled MENU): the root rows RESUME / STATS / CONTROLS / SETTINGS / QUIT read legibly with exactly ONE row visibly marked as selected (a cursor marker and brighter tone), an ESC hint line reads on the panel, and the world stays readable BEHIND the veil (floor grid, bodies, or HUD bars still discernible - the veil dims, it never blacks out the frame). A CONTROLS-titled sheet frame reads as a key reference: rows of key glyphs paired with action labels, including a movement row and a menu row. If no menu panel appears anywhere in the reel, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where a STATS-titled menu panel is on camera (es ESTADÍSTICAS / pt ESTATÍSTICAS): a pack header reads legibly - a LEVEL line carrying the level number plus an XP progress pair current/threshold (or MAX at cap), and a session-XP line - followed by one row per pack body (player 1 / player 2 / player 3), each pairing an HP current/max readout with a damage integer, and below them a REACH line showing a spell-growth tier as a dash-joined distance sequence (with a NEXT L<n> marker while a higher tier exists). A dead body's row (if any) explicitly carries the DEAD word in a dimmer tone. The HP pairs on the panel must be CONSISTENT with the HUD bars visible in the same frame (a full bar never pairs with a near-zero readout), an ESC hint line reads on the panel, and the world stays readable behind the veil. If no STATS panel appears anywhere in the reel, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where TWO OR MORE frames show the menu panel open: the world visibly ADVANCES between them behind the veil - an enemy has moved, an HP bar has dropped, a corpse or combat effect has appeared or resolved; the world region must NOT read as frozen/identical behind the open panel (a paused world under the menu is exactly the failure this check exists to catch). If fewer than two menu-open frames exist in the reel, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where a SETTINGS-titled menu panel is on camera (es AJUSTES / pt OPÇÕES): LANGUAGE, WINDOW SCALE, and FULLSCREEN rows read legibly, each showing a current value after a colon (e.g. EN, AUTO, OFF). If runtime audio is available, the same panel also shows per-bus VOLUME rows plus a MUTE row, each with a value; if audio is absent those rows must be absent rather than fake controls. Exactly ONE row is visibly selected (cursor marker and brighter tone), an ESC hint reads on the panel, and the world stays readable behind the veil. If no SETTINGS panel appears anywhere in the reel, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where frames show a safe hub interior (HUB 1 camp or ZONE 7): a small SAFE text chip on a quiet dark backing reads at the top-left status block just below the LEVEL strip, present in EVERY safe-zone frame including frames long after any zone banner has faded (persistent state, not a transient banner), and absent in every frame of unsafe zones (e.g. ZONE 3). Door tiles between zones of DIFFERING safety carry a thin static frame outlining the tile: seen from inside the safe zone, doors to unsafe zones frame in dark ember red (a quiet 'beyond this = danger' signpost, dimmer and thinner than the hot red-edge attack telegraph and never pulsing); seen from the unsafe side, the door back into safety frames in calm mint green ('reach that door = safety'), distinct from the solid gold way fill it surrounds, the pale green-white respawn tell, and the green vat fixture. Doors between two zones of the SAME safety carry no frame. If no safe zone and no safety-differing door appears in this replay, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where consecutive frames dwell beside the bright green totem fixture mid-bridge (a green station tile on wood planks over dark water): at least one such frame shows a vivid green square ring expanding around that fixture (the heal pulse), clearly wider than the fixture tile and distinct in color from the rust taunt ring family. If no frame shows the pack dwelling beside the green mid-bridge fixture, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where frames show the compact two-chamber fixture zone TEST 2 (a small single-screen room grid): its outer boundary walls read as one very dark near-black solid color while interior chamber wall segments read clearly RED - two visibly DIFFERENT wall colors coexist in the SAME frame, both drawn as solid square blocking tiles of identical size (neither reads as floor tint, decor, or a station fixture). If this replay never shows the TEST 2 fixture zone, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where ZONE 3 frames show the deep channel (a band of vivid deep-blue tiles): the channel's margins carry ORANGE coral blocks - two visibly DIFFERENT wall colors coexist in the same frame (rust-brown boundary rock and orange coral), both solid square blocking tiles - and no body ever stands ON a deep-blue channel tile in any frame (the water is a void, not a floor). Lighter walkable lane tiles (fords) may interrupt the channel; bodies there are lawful. If no ZONE 3 channel frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where ZONE 3 (district_two) combat frames are present: hostile bodies read in TWO new tones distinct from the pale-bone humans of other zones - a pale green-tinted minion family (several per fight) and, near the channel crossing, a single larger-presence PINK body (the guardian; it moves visibly slower and telegraphs long). At least one frame shows a green-tinted hostile adjacent to a pack body mid-fight. If no ZONE 3 combat frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where ZONE 3 (district_two) frames show open ground away from the channel: the floor reads as a dark blue-grey submerged plain with visible green algae patches (walkable, textured with sparse ripple motif marks) and occasional tan bank clusters - clearly distinct at a glance from ZONE 2's warm dark canyon and from HUB 1's warm gray. The ZONE 3 banner is legible when shown. If no such frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where ZONE 5 (low_quay, MUSGO) combat frames are present: GREEN mushroom-cap hostiles (small thin-stem caps and broad heavy caps — no other body family owns saturated fungus green) close to melee range on the pack; a struck pack body may pulse sick-green (poison) and a struck mushroom flashes red-brown, never pink or white. If no ZONE 5 combat frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where ZONE 5 (low_quay, MUSGO: loam floor with dark-green moss, pale stone walls) frames show the boss (BOSS 1, a pale-bone human wearing the cream BOSS 1 nameplate): he holds the walled vault to the east and his nameplate reads separated from the moss by its dark halo; in the frames after his engagement stamp the line BOSS 1 SPAWNED is legible in the banner slot. Green mushroom bodies (even when flashing red from a hit) are spore hostiles, NOT the boss. If no nameplated boss body or stamp frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where frames show ZONE 5 (dark loam floor carpeted with darker green MOSS tiles, pale stone-grey walls, torches in a walled 15x17 vault to the east): the moss reads as a living carpet distinct from the loam, the vault's walls read as one continuous stone enclosure with exactly two openings, and green mushroom-cap enemies (small caps / broad heavy caps) read as a family distinct from the pale bone humans. If no ZONE 5 frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where frames show a MEDUSA TOWER floor (DUNGEON 2, 3 or 4: a round rust-red ring wall on dark rock, grey stone floor inside, straight rust-red interior walls forming a spiral or divider, torches on the walls): everything walkable sits INSIDE the ring, the rock outside reads as a second darker wall class, and the interior walls read as continuous barriers a player must walk around (no gaps mid-wall). Violet serpent-family bodies (coil / hooded / whip) read distinct from cyan stingers and pink wardens. If no tower frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where frames show BRASA (DUNGEON 5, 6 or 7: near-black basalt floor, dark brown-red walls, scattered bright orange LAVA tiles, rising ember sparks, torches): the lava pools read as glowing hazards distinct from the floor and from gate gold, red-orange ember bodies (bull-wedge charger / round brazier with heat crown / tall pillar with one burning eye) read as one hot family distinct from the pack's orange, and any aura ring reads as a steady breathing square around its bearer (not an expanding pulse). If no BRASA frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When a hostile CHARGE or BEAM winds up, its lane is drawn on the FLOOR (dark red squares along the run for a charge; dark ember squares along the line for a beam) BEFORE the strike, and the strike itself paints the same lane in a brighter hot orange; the ground lane reads as 'this lane is about to be hit' and is distinct from the body flare and from volley brackets. If no charge/beam frame is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where a boss NAMEPLATE (cream BOSS N text with a dark halo, above a body) is on camera: small rust squares sit under the name, one per phase, exactly one filled — the fight arc reads at body scale. A body without a nameplate is not a boss (pink/red-flashing hostiles are hurt bodies). If no nameplated boss is present, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Ways out are SIGNPOSTED: an open door/hole/stairs tile on camera carries a soft gold glow that breathes (never on a shut, dark-slab way); an open way OFF camera is announced by a small gold ARROWHEAD clamped to the viewport edge pointing toward it (up to four). The arrowhead is a triangle on the screen edge - not a square (ally edge pips are kit-colored squares), not the gold chevron that points DOWN over the possessed body, not a world-anchored gem. If the reel shows no zone with an off-screen open way, judge only the glow; if no transition tile is ever on camera either, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.
